nodes.label: Mostrico Security Rules (local-only, no secrets to browser)
nodes.norm_label: mostrico security rules (local-only, no secrets to browser)
nodes.rationale: Mostrico touches Bitcoin, Nostr, Lightning and a local mostro-cli database, so contributions must advance without weakening security boundaries: keep the app local-only, never read or return user secrets to the browser, use allowlisted argument builders instead of arbitrary command execution, open ~/.mcli/mcli.db read-only, and never make Lightning payments or fiat transfers from the app.

nodes.label: Single Writer Per Identity
nodes.rationale: Different orders share the derivation counter, so a per-order lock is not enough and the CLI offers no distributed coordinator; a single active writer per identity with durable index reservation and fencing is required. An external Mobile client importing the same seed is not controlled by this lock, so the initial policy is one active writer per identity with explicit transfer of control.

nodes.label: fiatsent Is a Declaration, Not a Transfer
nodes.norm_label: fiatsent is a declaration, not a transfer
nodes.rationale: fiatsent only tells Mostro the fiat was already paid; it never executes a bank transfer. Therefore the UI requires an explicit checkbox confirmation ('Confirmo que ya envie el pago fiat') and never automates the fiat bank transfer.

nodes.label: Local-First Architecture
nodes.rationale: The Mostro CLI stores the user's identity locally and derives trade keys from its mnemonic/database. A hosted website that remotely controls a user's CLI would create unnecessary custody/security risks, so the MVP runs locally on 127.0.0.1 with a Next.js server wrapping mostro-cli; the browser never executes the CLI.
